title: Variant-aware automated upgrades for private control plane with progressive health gates
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Objective: Build an automated, variant-aware control plane upgrade pipeline for Private (VPC) deployments that performs progressive canary waves with automated health gates, deterministic rollback, and Terraform-driven IaC orchestration. This ticket covers: 1) Terraform module changes and version pinning strategy for control plane components; 2) a state-machine-based orchestrator that runs staged waves against host groups; 3) health checks and SLO/metric based gating; 4) safe rollback automation and human-in-loop pause points; 5) runbooks, tests, and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules can create an immutable control-plane instance set with versioned module inputs and a toggle for "variant" mapping per customer
Orchestrator runs canary waves (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%) across control-plane variants and respects max-concurrency and disruption windows
Automated gates evaluate latency P50/P95, API error-rate, reconciliation-failure-rate, and KV-cache miss-rate; gates fail -> automatic rollback to previous stable version
All changes are reproducible from IaC and documented runbook exists in the private-controlplane-runbook Confluence page
End-to-end test harness that simulates traffic shaping and introduces synthetic faults to validate rollback triggers
Monitoring dashboards and alerts created: canary-upgrade-health, canary-rollforward, canary-rollback
implementation_notes: Design decision: use variant-aware upgrades instead of a pure region wave — some customers require different control-plane build variants (k8s runtime differences, pkg versions). We'll map variants in Terraform via a 'variant_map' input that resolves to instance profiles.

Trade-off: tighter gating (more metrics and longer observation windows) reduces regression risk but increases total upgrade time. Default policy will be conservative; customers may opt-in for faster waves via control-plane policy flags.

Terraform approach: add 'controlplane_release' object to modules with fields: version, image_tag, variant_label, rollout_policy_ref. Store current/desired version in state for drift detection rather than ad-hoc patching.

Orchestrator: implement as a small Go service that reads desired-state from Terraform outputs + a separate 'upgrade-manifest' in S3/secure storage. Use a step-function style state machine with idempotent steps and leader-election for HA.

Health checks: lightweight probe (admin/healthz), reconciliation lag (controller loop duration), API 5xx/s, auth-failure-rate, kv-cache hit ratio. Each metric has threshold + observation window stored in policy. Use Prometheus rules and Loki for log sampling.

Rollback criteria: any gate failing for two consecutive observation windows -> automatic rollback. Rollback runs via Terraform applying previous version inputs with a dry-run validation step and safety hold if > X nodes changed (configurable).
Human-in-loop: after 10% wave, open a manual approval step by default. This can be overridden by 'auto_approve' flag for non-sensitive customers or test clusters.
Compatibility: integrates with existing VPC control plane canary orchestration primitives but will not replace tenant-specific upgrade scripts until validated for 3 customers in pilot.
Security: upgrade manifest and Terraform state must be encrypted; KMS keys scoped per-customer. Security review required prior to GA.
tasks: Module: add 'controlplane_release' input and variant_map to terraform/modules/controlplane (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/PR-422)
Orchestrator: prototype Go state machine service with step persistence (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-orchestrator/PR-17)
Health rules: author Prometheus alerting and evaluation dashboards (Grafana: /d/canary-upgrade-health)
Runbook: draft upgrade runbook and rollback checklist in Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Private+Control+Plane+Upgrade+Runbook)
E2E tests: add simulated-customer harness in testinfra that can throttle and inject 5xxs during waves
Pilot: run on 3 pilot customers (internal-staging, pilot-cust-01, pilot-cust-02) and collect metrics for 2 weeks before broader rollout
risks: Terraform state drift: if customers have local modifications outside our modules, automated rollback may not cleanly revert. Mitigation: pre-flight validation and pre-apply dry-run with a 'drift_report' sent to customer admins.

Blast radius from failed rollback: partial rollbacks can leave control plane heterogeneous. Mitigation: orchestrator ensures idempotent steps and includes a 'quarantine' policy to isolate impacted nodes behind a circuit breaker.
Metric noise causing false positives: transient SLO spikes may trigger rollback unnecessarily. Mitigation: require two consecutive windows and correlated multi-signal failure before rollback.
Secrets exposure if manifest storage misconfigured: require KMS encryption and RBAC checks on manifest bucket; include automated linter in CI to block misconfiguration.

2026-03-10: Health check thresholds initially proposed by SRE team: p95_latency < 350ms, api_5xx_rate < 0.5%, reconciler_lag < 5s. These were iterated after synthetic fault runs.
